title: Forbidden Psalm - Using battlemats to suggest narrative, and customizing your experience
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qMz0UbGJq4Y

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to *Forbidden Psalm*, the Mork Borg skirmish game, with a follow-up that is half after-action report and half table-craft. First the warband: Savannah and the Ragged Tigers, each member built from stat bumps, a flaw and a feat — Savannah herself terrified of monsters, Risen the Forgiven limping out on two HP, Kamak the Pew Pew accumulating tragedies every time a spell fizzles, each one stacking the calamity roll further against him.

The real subject is the battlemat as narrative engine. Sent by Riprix to gather corpse-fungus, he built a cemetery-into-sewer layout, then noticed his mat had three distinct exits — and turned that geography into a branching campaign. The natural cave leads to scenario two's animal cultists; the mausoleum to the necromancer of scenario five; the crypt stairs to *Mort Safe*, which, being a dungeon rather than a skirmish, he intends to play instead as a pen-and-paper crawl using Solitary Defilement's rules, complete with four rolled special rooms and a corpse collector guarding the master crypt. Riprix's hovel becomes the hub you return to between them.

He closes with home-made paper minis drawn fat-Sharpie style — heads, torsos, deliberate crops — arguing Mork Borg's aesthetic actively invites the amateur hand.

----

Daniel let the physical layout of his mat decide where the campaign could go, rather than the other way round. Have you ever let the table dictate the story — and did what emerged beat what you would have planned?
